messages:
alex chen: Heads-up — CI failures after I added sm_90 to the fatbin list. Build passes locally but CI artifacts are huge (~210MB -> 430MB for libkernels.so) and then runners OOM during upload. Anyone run into this when widening nvcc arch list?
maria singh: yup. adding additional sm_* codegen produces multiple device code blobs (fatbin) and binary explodes. We saw this when we added sm_86 earlier. CI runners have limited disk/transfer budget.
jonathan park: quick theory: we're compiling both native SASS for each sm and PTX. If nvcc emits SASS for sm_80 and sm_90 plus PTX, size multiplies. Consider using PTX for newer archs and native for one or two shipping targets.
sophia reed: +1. We had a similar tradeoff: keep sm_80 and sm_86 as sm targets, and use code=compute_90 (PTX) for Hopper to allow forward-compat without shipping SASS. That keeps bundle small and still runs on new cards.
ryan o'neil: FWIW, CI matrix currently is: sm_70, sm_75, sm_80, sm_86, sm_90 — that's five targets. Maybe overkill for release artifacts. We can keep full matrix for test builds but produce a slim release artifact.
alex chen: sample nvcc line causing bloat:
```
nvcc -O3 -Xcompiler "-fPIC" -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -gencode arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 -lineinfo -Xptxas -v -o libkernels.so
```
Switching the last gencode to `code=compute_90` reduces size a lot.
maria singh: also check ptxas register pressure. `-Xptxas -v` shows register/use and spilling; sometimes adding sm targets increases constant pool duplication. We should strip debug/lineinfo for release (`--strip` or remove `-lineinfo`).
jonathan park: For CI/toolchain changes I propose:
- Build matrix: test builds for all supported SMs (70/75/80/86/90)
- Release artifact: compile with minimal native SASS (sm_80, sm_86), everything else `code=compute_XX` (PTX)
- Update packaging step to run `cuobjdump --list-device-symbols` and `cuobjdump -ptx` checks to validate tiny PTX presence
- Use actions/cache for the CUDA toolkit and sccache for host obj caching
sophia reed: +1. Also add a lint that fails if we accidentally add `code=sm_XX` for more than N targets (N=2?) in the release build.
ryan o'neil: CI practicals: runner disk limit is 14GB on ephemeral. When we had fatbins for many archs the shared lib + conda env exceeded cache upload limits (timeout). Splitting the library into smaller per-arch wheel artifacts could help (publish per-arch wheels) but that complicates pip packaging.
alex chen: Bazel note: our CUDA toolchain args come from --define=cuda_compute_capabilities. We'll need to change the default to emit PTX form for higher entries: something like `--define cuda_arch_list=80,86,compute_90`? We'll write a tiny wrapper that translates to `-gencode` flags.
maria singh: CI script snippet to generate flags (bash):
```
# generate nvcc gencode flags
from_list=(80 86 90)
for v in "${from_list[@]}"; do
  if [[ "$v" -ge 90 ]]; then
    echo "-gencode arch=compute_${v},code=compute_${v}";
  else
    echo "-gencode arch=compute_${v},code=sm_${v}";
  fi;
done
```
This keeps sm* for <=86 and PTX for >=90.
jonathan park: We should also audit our container base image. Newer libcudnn/cuda toolkits change default PTX compatibility levels. Lock the CUDA toolkit version in CI docker and add `nvcc --ptxas-options=-v` sanity step.
ci-bot: Build #4218 failed: artifacts exceed size limit (430MB > 300MB). See https://ci.redwood.ai/build/4218
alex chen: Re-ran with trimmed arch list (80 + 86 native, 90 PTX) — package dropped to 170MB. Uploaded fine. Pushed a PR to reduce default release archs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/182
sophia reed: We should also add a post-link check in artifact job that runs `nm -C libkernels.so | grep __device__` to estimate duplication, and `cuobjdump --dump-elf` to inspect fatbin sections.
ryan o'neil: One more thing: static linking vs shared linking affects size. If we link libkernels statically into python wheel it multiplies. Prefer shared libs for many deployments.
maria singh: Action items:
- alex chen: update CI wrapper + PR merged to toolchain defaults (WIP)
- jonathan park: add GitHub Actions matrix job for device smoke tests (A100, H100 emulated) — ensure we run at least one real-device test per PR
- sophia reed: add lint rule to fail large fatbins in release build
- ryan o'neil: update infra docs about artifact size limits and per-arch publishing tradeoffs

alex chen: thanks — I'll link the build logs and a short writeup in the RFC follow-up. If anyone wants to see the before/after lib dumps I can attach them to the PR.
